sections.content: If you're searching for real estate deals in Syracuse NY, you've landed on one of the most overlooked markets in the entire Northeast. While cities like Buffalo and Albany get more attention, Syracuse quietly offers some of the best fundamentals for investors: low entry prices, steady rental demand, and a growing economy anchored by universities and healthcare. Whether you're a first-time investor or a seasoned pro expanding your portfolio, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know. If you're just getting started, bookmark our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide as a companion resource.
Syracuse NY Real Estate Market Overview

Syracuse is the fifth-largest city in New York State, home to roughly 148,000 people. Onondaga County adds another 320,000+ residents to the metro area. The city sits at the crossroads of I-81 and I-90, making it a regional hub for healthcare, education, and logistics. Syracuse University and SUNY Upstate Medical University are two of the largest employers, creating a stable base of renters and a relatively recession-resistant local economy. That combination — affordable prices plus consistent demand — is exactly what real estate investors look for.
Average Home Prices in Syracuse

As of 2024, the median home price in the city of Syracuse sits around $140,000 to $160,000, depending on the neighborhood and property type. The broader Onondaga County median is closer to $195,000. Compare that to the national median of roughly $420,000, and you immediately see why investors from higher-cost markets like New York City, Boston, and New Jersey have been paying attention. Single-family rentals in Syracuse commonly list between $900 and $1,400 per month, while multi-family properties — especially duplexes and triplexes — can generate gross rents of $1,800 to $3,000 per month. The math for cash flow works here in ways it simply doesn't in many coastal markets.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Syracuse

Not all zip codes are created equal. Syracuse has a mix of high-performing investor neighborhoods and areas that require more due diligence. Here's a breakdown of the most active zones for deal-finding.

items: Eastwood (13206): A working-class neighborhood on the east side with strong rental demand and relatively stable property values. Median prices hover around $130,000 to $155,000 with solid cash flow for buy-and-hold investors.

Near Westside / Tipperary Hill (13204): One of the most improved areas in the city, with active community development programs and rising home values. Great for flippers who buy right and move quickly.

University Hill / Strathmore (13210): Located near Syracuse University, this corridor has consistent demand from students, faculty, and hospital staff. Multi-family properties here can produce strong cap rates.
Sedgwick (13203): An up-and-coming neighborhood seeing renovation activity and investor interest. Properties are priced low enough to leave room for both rehab costs and profit margin.

Dewitt and Fayetteville (suburban): Suburbs in Onondaga County with higher-income renters, better school districts, and properties in the $200,000 to $280,000 range. Lower yields but lower vacancy risk.
North Side (13208): High density of affordable multi-family properties. Experienced investors are finding 2-4 unit buildings here at prices that generate 8% to 10%+ cap rates when managed well.

Markets like the Near Westside are changing fast — a comp from 18 months ago may no longer reflect accurate ARV. Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Syracuse
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in the Syracuse market. Motivated sellers — often dealing with probate properties, tax delinquency, or inherited homes in disrepair — are willing to accept below-market offers in exchange for speed and simplicity. Assignment fees in the $5,000 to $15,000 range are common on single-family wholesale deals. For investors new to this strategy, read our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand how the process works before jumping in. The key to successful wholesaling here is building a strong buyers list — local flippers and landlords who move fast when the right deal hits their inbox.
Fix and Flip

Syracuse offers realistic flip margins for investors who know how to manage rehab costs. A typical flip scenario might look like this: buy a distressed property in Eastwood for $85,000, invest $40,000 in renovations, and sell for $155,000 to $165,000. That leaves a gross profit of $30,000 to $40,000 before holding costs and closing fees. The key is accurate ARV analysis and tight contractor management. Rehab labor costs in Syracuse are lower than in major metro areas, which helps protect your margin. Always run your numbers through a deal analyzer before committing — the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) at aiwholesail.com is a quick way to stress-test your assumptions.
Buy and Hold Rentals

This is arguably the strongest play in Syracuse right now. Low purchase prices combined with consistent rental demand from university students, healthcare workers, and young professionals create a favorable environment for long-term cash flow. A duplex purchased for $150,000 renting for $1,600 per month total can produce a cap rate above 7% after expenses — a number that's nearly impossible to find in markets like Boston or Philadelphia. Multi-family properties in the 2-4 unit range are especially popular with out-of-state investors because they spread vacancy risk across multiple units.

"The best real estate markets aren't always the ones on the news. They're the ones with steady jobs, affordable prices, and more buyers waiting than there are good deals available." — Common wisdom among experienced buy-and-hold investors
Syracuse Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Rising demand from out-of-state investors: Syracuse is increasingly appearing on investor radar as coastal markets price out smaller buyers. This is gradually compressing cap rates in the best neighborhoods.

Micron Technology investment: The $100 billion Micron semiconductor plant planned for Clay, NY (just north of Syracuse) is expected to bring 9,000 direct jobs and tens of thousands of indirect jobs to the region. This is a potential game-changer for property values and rental demand over the next 5 to 10 years.
Tax delinquency pipeline: Onondaga County regularly releases tax-delinquent properties through the Land Bank, creating a steady stream of below-market acquisition opportunities for patient investors.
Tight inventory: Like most U.S. markets, Syracuse has low housing inventory, which is supporting prices even as interest rates remain elevated nationwide.
Revitalization programs: City-funded renovation grants and programs targeting specific corridors are making previously overlooked neighborhoods more investable.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors
Many of the best investors in the Syracuse market don't live there. Buying remotely is absolutely possible, but it requires the right team and systems. Here's how to approach it strategically.

items: Build your local team first: Find a Syracuse-based real estate agent who works with investors, a reliable property manager (expect fees of 8% to 10% of gross rent), a local contractor for inspections and rehab estimates, and a real estate attorney familiar with NY landlord-tenant law.

Use the Onondaga County Land Bank: This public entity sells tax-foreclosed properties at below-market prices with the goal of neighborhood revitalization. It's one of the best sources of legitimate below-market deals in the county.

Target off-market deals: The most profitable deals rarely hit the MLS. Direct mail, driving for dollars, and networking with local wholesalers are proven strategies. Learn more in our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Understand New York landlord-tenant law: NY is a tenant-friendly state. Eviction timelines can be lengthy, so screen tenants carefully and build eviction costs into your risk analysis.

Analyze every deal with discipline: Emotional buying is the fastest way to lose money. Before submitting any offer, run a full deal analysis. Read [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) for a step-by-step framework.
Visit before you buy (at least once): Even experienced remote investors benefit from walking properties and neighborhoods in person before committing significant capital to a new market.

sections.content: Pro Tip: The Micron plant in Clay, NY could be the single biggest economic catalyst this region has seen in decades. If you're evaluating long-term buy-and-hold investments, properties within 15 to 20 minutes of the Micron site may see above-average appreciation over the next several years. Don't wait until the headlines make it obvious — the smart money moves early.

Syracuse is not a flashy market. It won't generate the social media buzz of a Phoenix or a Nashville. But for investors focused on fundamentals — cash flow, affordability, and long-term stability — real estate deals in Syracuse NY offer genuine opportunity. The city has the institutions, the workforce, and the incoming economic investment to support a healthy rental market for years to come.
